about.description:
edge-tts lets Python code and the command line use Microsoft Edge's
online text-to-speech service, without needing Edge, Windows, or an API
key. It can write audio and word-boundary subtitle files, list the
available voices, and stream synthesized speech.

Two entry points are installed: ``edge-tts`` for synthesis, and
``edge-playback`` which plays the result back. ``edge-playback``
additionally requires the ``mpv`` media player on PATH at runtime; it is
not declared as a dependency because the ``edge-tts`` entry point and the
Python API do not need it.
about.summary: Python client for Microsoft Edge's online text-to-speech service

name: edge-tts
raw_meta_yaml:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/prefix-dev/recipe-format/main/schema.json
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "7.2.8"

package:
  name: edge-tts
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://pypi.org/packages/source/e/edge-tts/edge_tts-${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: fcf185a0d527a0d2d003f9d5841facc1d5e0e7b3b88d5df9c32990402c6b8cd0

build:
  number: 0
  noarch: python
  script: ${{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . -vv --no-deps --no-build-isolation
  python:
    entry_points:
      - edge-tts = edge_tts.__main__:main
      - edge-playback = edge_playback.__main__:_main

requirements:
  host:
    - python ${{ python_min }}.*
    - setuptools
    - pip
  run:
    - python >=${{ python_min }}
    - aiohttp >=3.8.0,<4.0.0
    - certifi >=2023.11.17
    - tabulate >=0.4.4,<1.0.0
    - typing_extensions >=4.1.0,<5.0.0

tests:
  - python:
      imports:
        - edge_tts
        - edge_playback
      pip_check: true
      python_version:
        - ${{ python_min }}.*
        - "*"
  - requirements:
      run:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
    script:
      - edge-tts --help

about:
  homepage: https://github.com/rany2/edge-tts
  repository: https://github.com/rany2/edge-tts
  license: LGPL-3.0-only
  license_file: LICENSE
  summary: Python client for Microsoft Edge's online text-to-speech service
  description: |
    edge-tts lets Python code and the command line use Microsoft Edge's
    online text-to-speech service, without needing Edge, Windows, or an API
    key. It can write audio and word-boundary subtitle files, list the
    available voices, and stream synthesized speech.

    Two entry points are installed: ``edge-tts`` for synthesis, and
    ``edge-playback`` which plays the result back. ``edge-playback``
    additionally requires the ``mpv`` media player on PATH at runtime; it is
    not declared as a dependency because the ``edge-tts`` entry point and the
    Python API do not need it.

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - rxm7706
